proposals.evidence: Full truṭyati includes Prakrit tuṭṭai/ṭuṭṭai and the associated tuṭṭa “broken”, with Lahnda/Punjabi ṭuṭṭ-, Nepali ṭuṭnu, Bihari ṭūṭal and Hindi ṭūṭā. These whole survey responses retain that break stem with regional infinitive or participial morphology (-eko, -la/-lo, -yā/-eā); the dental/retroflex and aspiration notation is preserved. Responses containing go/be auxiliaries, a negative particle, or two stems are excluded.

proposals.evidence: The bhajyate article explicitly gives Lahnda bhajjaṇ and Punjabi bhajjṇā “be broken/flee”, contrasting the separate g-retaining bhagna branch. These Pothwari paj- broken/infinitive responses match the former stem with the regional voiceless outcome of initial voiced aspiration; the j is retained. This is a bhajj- family analysis, leaving the original loss of aspiration/tone realization at the survey’s recorded level, and it does not cover the SSNP y-spelled forms awaiting font checks.
